title: A three-branch union inside an array element, with its data in a child column
rationale: The shape reconstructArrayOfRecords had never had an arm for. Its Step 3 field dispatch recognised exactly three things - flat column present, RECORD, ARRAY - and unwrapNullable, its only union handling, collapses only [null,T]. A union of arity three therefore arrived still typed UNION, matched nothing, and fell off the end into handleMissingField, which saw a NULL branch and wrote a plain null. The union field's default is deliberately OMITTED so the null is a real Java null and this row does not entangle with the JsonProperties.NULL_VALUE finding recorded on avro-union-of-records-overlapping-fields. Two elements rather than one, so a repair that fixes only element 0 is caught.
catchesBugClass: A whole branch of a type dispatch that was never written, producing total silence: no exception, no log at any level, and a structurally valid record whose field is simply empty. It is the array-element mirror of the union defect the corpus already records at the top level, and it re-arms if anyone narrows the arity guard.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the MIXED-branch case, where the flattener emits BOTH a bare items_meta column and an items_meta_src child column and the flat-column arm wins for both elements - that needs its own document and has one beside this. It says nothing about a union with TWO record branches, which is information-theoretically unresolvable from column names and is pinned as a throw in AvroReconstructorArrayElementUnionTest rather than here. And it does not cover a multi-branch union at the TOP level, which goes through reconstructUnionValue and is untouched by this repair.

predicted.detail: The new array-element union arm computes the available child columns, finds exactly one record branch whose fields intersect them, and dispatches to the index-aware nested-record helper, so meta.src comes back for both elements.

measurementNote: PRE-FIX BEHAVIOUR, MEASURED VERBATIM AS A JUnit FAILURE BEFORE THE REPAIR. AvroReconstructorArrayElementUnionTest.threeBranchUnionInsideArrayElementKeepsItsRecordBranch, run against the unfixed code: 'flat={items_sku=["a","b"], items_meta_src=["web","pos"]} back={items=[{sku=a, meta=null}, {sku=b, meta=null}]} ==> expected: not <null>'. NEVER-IMPLEMENTED GAP, NOT A REGRESSION - and this matters because the obvious repair is the wrong one. unwrapUnion, whose 'first non-null branch at any arity' behaviour looks like the missing piece, had FOUR calls and ZERO declarations through ef625f2 and a declaration with zero callers from cad816b, so it never executed in any revision and nothing was lost. NoDeadPrivateMethodsInTheFormerlySuppressedClassesTest forbids re-adding it by name. HONEST NARROWING OF THE FILING, also measured: the SILENT drop is specific to unions that CONTAIN a null branch. With no null branch, handleMissingField falls to its switch default, log.warns, never sets the field, and GenericRecordBuilder.build() throws AvroRuntimeException - already loud, just uselessly so.
